claims.statement: Server startup loads configuration, constructs the two-version Signal Siege production registry, connects PostgreSQL, applies migrations, optionally constructs the provider runtime, starts persona synchronization, serves Axum with graceful shutdown, and aborts the listener task when serving ends.
The health route executes SELECT 1 against the shared PostgreSQL pool and returns HTTP 200 with an ok document only when the query yields 1; other results return HTTP 503 with a degraded document.
The initial migration already establishes separate accounts, revocable account sessions, and personas with case-insensitive unique usernames and handles.
Account-session rows store only a token hash plus expiry, last-used, revocation, and creation timestamps.
Account registration uses a thin Axum POST /v1/accounts handler with a 1 KiB body limit, delegates validation and insertion to the account module, and delegates Argon2id work to shared credentials.
The account domain canonicalizes usernames to a bounded ASCII namespace and accepts passwords only from 12 through 128 bytes.
Shared credential code hashes passwords off the async executor with OS-random salts and Argon2id v19 parameters m=19456 KiB, t=2, and p=1 before registration persistence.
The canonical username format is enforced by a forward migration while the named case-insensitive unique index remains the authority for duplicate registration conflicts.
Registration and login share a four-permit semaphore before their blocking Argon2id work, and missing-account login performs dummy hash work before the generic credential failure.
When MFA is disabled, device-session creation issues ogs1_ tokens with 32 OS-random bytes, stores only SHA-256(token), and returns the raw token once in a no-store response.

Session issuance sets a 30-day absolute expiry, and Bearer authentication advances last use only when the token is unrevoked, inside its seven-day idle limit and absolute expiry, and belongs to an active account.
Session inventory and revocation derive account ownership from the authenticated token; listing filters by that account and revocation predicates on both account and session IDs.
The device-session migration adds bounded device names and requires every stored token digest to contain exactly 32 bytes.
Persona handles are trimmed and ASCII-lowercased into a 3–24 byte namespace, profile text is bounded and control-safe, and a forward migration rejects noncanonical handles from every database writer.
Persona create, inventory, and edit operations authenticate the device session; inventory filters by the derived account ID and edits predicate on both persona and account IDs.
Public persona lookup canonicalizes an exact handle and maps invalid and absent handles to the same not-found result.
Persona persistence rows are narrowed through a seven-field domain model and an explicit seven-field transport DTO, so account ownership and session data are unavailable to response serialization.
Bearer parsing accepts structurally valid ogs1_ and legacy bbs1_ tokens, hashes the exact presented token, and applies the same account-status, expiry, idle, and revocation controls.
OGS_BIND_ADDRESS takes precedence over the transitional BBS_BIND_ADDRESS fallback, both development defaults remain loopback-only, and startup also requires a valid OGS_MFA_ENCRYPTION_KEY.
Health documents identify the service as omarchy-gaming-system while retaining database-aware healthy and degraded states.
OGS_MFA_ENCRYPTION_KEY must decode from unpadded base64url to 32 bytes, and AES-256-GCM protects each recoverable TOTP secret with a random nonce and the account UUID as associated data.

Beginning MFA enrollment requires an authenticated session and current password, stores a replaceable encrypted pending secret, and confirmation must use a valid TOTP within ten minutes before enabling the authenticator and returning ten recovery codes.

Password login for an MFA-enabled account creates an independent five-minute hashed challenge instead of a session; at most ten unexpired challenges may coexist, and excess issuance returns a rate limit without invalidating live challenges.
Challenge completion locks challenge, account, and authenticator rows and atomically consumes the selected challenge and TOTP step or recovery code before issuing a device session.
Five failed factor attempts lock the authenticator for five minutes across challenges, while successful factor use clears the failure state and prevents TOTP-step or recovery-code replay.

Disabling MFA requires a valid device session, current password, and valid TOTP or unused recovery code, then removes the authenticator and all dependent recovery codes and outstanding challenges without revoking existing device sessions.

Forward migration 0005 adds one TOTP authenticator per account, hashed single-use recovery codes, and hashed expiring login challenges with database constraints on ciphertext, nonce, digest, device-name, attempt, and expiry fields.
Every connection or block operation authenticates a device session and constrains the acting persona to the derived account before reading private inventory or mutating pair state.
One canonical UUID-ordered row represents each pending or accepted persona pair, with requester/addressee direction retained until the addressee atomically accepts it.

Persona blocks are private and directional; creating a block serializes on both persona rows and deletes any pending or accepted relationship in the same transaction, while unblock never restores prior state.
Connection and block responses embed only the existing public persona model, private inventories are owner-scoped, and unavailable state-creating targets use bounded non-disclosing errors.

A state-changing social, inbox, game-challenge, game-session, or game-command transaction appends each affected persona's typed retained synchronization event before the same transaction commits, while no-op and replay branches append nothing.

The owned-persona sync REST endpoint returns an empty baseline at the current cursor or bounded ascending retained events after a cursor and requires reset whenever retained continuity cannot be proved.

The owner-authenticated sync WebSocket emits ready, changed, or resync-required documents only; admission is capped per persona, account, and process, while Axum limits incoming frames and assembled messages to 1 KiB.

Prepared sync sockets retain account and session UUIDs instead of raw tokens and reauthorize without touching last-used time before readiness, before hints, and periodically, closing on invalid sessions or database uncertainty.
Migration 0009 adds persona-local synchronization state and constrained typed retained events keyed by persona and positive event sequence.

Focused sync validation combines quota and cursor-continuity unit tests with six migrated PostgreSQL cases for mutation mapping, retention/reset, commit-only hints, real WebSocket authorization and decoder limits, principal quotas, and no-touch session lifecycle.

The database-free game runtime validates canonical manifests and exact versions, bounds object state and commands, and requires compiled commands to return a bounded snapshot plus an active or completed lifecycle.

Trusted game-session creation validates and initializes before writes, locks unique participant personas in canonical UUID order, persists the immutable version and ordered seats, and appends one minimal game-session invalidation per participant inside the caller's transaction.

Game-session reads authenticate the device session, require owned-persona participation, and return durable authority-tagged active or completed version-pinned state or provider projections without reinterpreting stored history through the current registry.

Forward migration 0010 adds canonical positive-version game sessions, revision-zero object snapshots, unique bounded persona seats, and a shaped game-session UUID variant in retained persona synchronization events.

Game validation combines runtime tests, ten Signal Siege v1/v2 rule tests, local catalog/body-limit checks, general PostgreSQL session cases, solo Signal Siege cases, and a production two-human challenge-to-terminal-session case.

A new participant command locks the owned session, resolves any receipt before lifecycle or revision admission, executes only active exact-version rules, and atomically commits state, lifecycle, completion time, one revision, the receipt, and minimal participant invalidations.

A matching command receipt compares actor, expected revision, and JSONB-semantic command identity and returns the stored revision, lifecycle, and state without rules execution or another event, including after completion.

Forward migration 0011 makes command identity session-wide, binds each receipt actor to a session participant, permits only one receipt per applied revision, and enforces one-step nonnegative object-state transitions.

Forward migration 0011 makes command identity session-wide, binds each receipt actor to a session participant, permits only one receipt per applied revision, and enforces one-step nonnegative object-state transitions.

Challenge creation authenticates and owner-scopes the challenger, accepts only an exact registered game version that admits two people, locks the connected pair, applies seven-day expiry and 100-per-direction pending limits, and persists the challenge, inbox message, and participant invalidations in one transaction.

A challenger-scoped idempotency UUID replays only the same immutable target and game identity, and exact retries return retained participant-authorized history without requiring the relationship or registry policy that applied to the first write.
Challenge inventory and detail expose only participant-visible public persona projections and resolve due pending rows into retained expired history before returning them.

Only the challenged persona may accept or decline and only the challenger may cancel; acceptance rechecks the connected pair and commits exact session creation, the accepted link, typed inbox history, and challenge, conversation, and session invalidations atomically.

Migration 0012 constrains challenge participants, identity, monotonic status/session/resolution shape, challenger-scoped idempotency, one equivalent pending request, typed inbox challenge references, and payload-minimal challenge synchronization events.

Solo start authenticates and owner-scopes the persona, serializes on its root, replays a durable exact request before current admission, accepts only one-human manifests, and atomically creates the seat-zero session, receipt, and minimal sync event under a 25-active cap.

Signal Siege v1 owns deterministic simultaneous strike, guard, and charge rules plus a state-derived bot, validates cross-field snapshot invariants, and selects completed status on core destruction or the twelve-round limit.

Forward migration 0013 adds consistent active/completed session timestamps, persists each command receipt's applied lifecycle, and adds persona-scoped idempotent solo-start receipts linked to real participants.

Signal Siege v2 admits exactly two human participants, starts at seat zero, alternates one authoritative strike, guard, or charge action per turn, validates cross-field state evidence, and completes on core destruction or the twenty-four-turn limit.

The QML game controller uses the bearer-owning onboarding controller only as a selected-persona request gateway, loads catalog and session or challenge inventories in serial bounded steps, and manually refetches durable REST state after commands and revision conflicts.

The QML game boundary validates exact manifest, challenge, participant, session, command, and Signal Siege v1/v2 cross-field envelopes before publishing a platform-owned presentation; invalid-session authority clears the bearer and all persona/game state.
